patterns.rationale: All five misses use SNOW-style whitespace steganography: each line of innocuous visible text carries a 7-bit (or longer) binary payload encoded as a sequence of tabs and spaces appended after the last visible character. The static layer never sees an injection keyword; the behavioral axes never see a trigger phrase. This pattern matches the structural fingerprint of that encoding: a non-whitespace anchor, optional leading whitespace, then an adjacent tab-space or space-tab pair (the smallest possible mixed unit) followed by 3+ more whitespace characters — a minimum total payload width of 5 chars. Any 7-bit SNOW sequence is guaranteed to contain at least one such pair, regardless of the specific bit values encoded, because a 7-char sequence mixing both character types cannot avoid producing an adjacent pair. The non-whitespace anchor `[^\s]` prevents the pattern from firing on leading indentation.
patterns.fp_notes: Could match a TSV/tab-aligned cell like `value\t   ` (tab + 3 spaces) or a source comment `func\t  //` if the trailing padding is long enough. Both require ≥5 chars of mixed trailing whitespace after visible content, which is uncommon in natural prose or formatted code; none of the known-good corpus files use tab characters in prose content areas.

semantic_note: The evasion is structural, not semantic — the injected bits live in trailing whitespace, not in words or phrases. A regex can detect the binary-encoding signature directly.
